newsitem.title: USA: PRESS DIGEST - New York Times front page - Feb 6.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - New York Times front page - Feb 6.

text.p: The New York Times reported the following stories on its front page Thursday:

* A $10.2 billion merger between Morgan Stanley Group and Dean Witter Discover & Co creates the world's largest securities firm, uniting Morgan Stanley's roster of elite corporate clients with Dean Witter's prowess in mutual funds and credit card services.
* Republicans react to President Clinton's State of the Union message a day later by criticizing Clinton's stances on a balanced budget amendment, campaign finance reform, welfare and education.
* U.S. citizens were much less enthralled by the O.J. Simpson civil trial than they were by the criminal trial, but their reaction to the verdict against him fell along similar racial lines.
* Switzerland's three largest banks have decided to create a fund with an initial worth of about $70 million for Holocaust victims.
* U.S. Ambassador to France Pamela Harriman dies at the age of 76 from complications of a cerebral hemorrhage.

* As a sign of the swelling number of immigrants in New York City, hundreds of Muslim students in the city's public schools are observing the Ramadan holiday, which began January 10 and ends Saturday night.

* News analysis: The crisis in Serbia is not over yet. Although President Slobodan Milosevic has decided to recognize the election victories of his opponents in 14 of Serbia's largest cities, the leaders of the opposition have yet to come up with a cohesive vision.
